name: evtx_carve
description: Recover event records from a blob that is not an event log: sweeps for ElfChnk chunk headers in unallocated space, a pagefile, a memory image or a truncated .evtx, checks that the 128 bytes after each ElfChnk signature are a chunk header (header size 0x80, the record offsets inside the 64 KiB, the first record number not past the last: python-evtx's ChunkHeader accepts garbage, so the tool checks), verifies each real chunk's own checksums and parses the records inside it. A signature that fails the header check is a problem line (a page, the whole list in a file) and counts only under candidates and signatures_rejected, never as a chunk found or parsed. Every matching record is kept with its whole XML in a file the answer names (written whenever anything was found); the inline records are the summary, without the XML unless with_xml is true. A repeated EventData name is kept as a list, not overwritten. chunk_limit (chunks parsed) and candidate_limit (places where the magic was found, built into a chunk or not) bound the work of one call, not the result: the sweep stops before the next one and resume_start is the offset to pass as start. The answer says the range asked for and the range examined, and sweep_complete means that range was swept, not that every record that ever existed was recovered. Problems are a page with the whole list in a file. A chunk whose checksums do not verify may still hold sound records, and is marked chunk_verified false. A carved record belongs to the channel it names, not to the file it was found in. SENSITIVE: carved records hold command lines, script text and arguments that can include a secret, and a pagefile or memory image can hold records of any process; run it as a job with secret_output: true when they may.

path.description: A raw blob: unallocated output, pagefile.sys, a memory image, or a damaged .evtx

contains.description: Keep only records whose XML contains this string, case-insensitive

start.description: Byte offset to start the sweep at (default 0)

max_bytes.description: Stop the sweep after this many bytes from start (at least 1)

chunk_limit.description: Chunks to parse in one call (default 200). When more remain the sweep stops before the next chunk and resume_start names the offset to pass as start; nothing before it is skipped

limit.description: Records shown inline (default 300, an inline page size); every matching record, with its XML, is in the file named by all_results

with_xml.description: Include each record's full XML in the inline records too (the file always has it)

candidate_limit.description: Chunk-magic hits to examine in one call (default 20000), whether or not each builds into a chunk; the sweep stops before the next and resume_start names where to carry on
